name: Daria Tanaka

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I’m with the independent Work Futures Panel. We have no ties to AI companies, employers, unions or government, and your answers are confidential. Tell me what your working day looks like.

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I am 58 and manage eight repair coordinators at a large residential property company. We receive reports of leaking roofs, damp rooms and broken lifts, then arrange a contractor and tell the tenant when someone will arrive. I have a bachelor’s degree and have done this for years; I am a capable, ordinary manager rather than the expert surveyor. I use an approved AI triage system every day to group urgent repairs, but I call a building caretaker when a photograph does not show how much water is actually coming in.

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: My partner runs a small bicycle-repair shop and our grown children live on their own. We rent our flat and have about three months of expenses saved. My salary is typical for this management job and covers our fixed rent and utilities, while the shop pays less regularly and helps with the rest. There are some other property-service offices nearby. I have not checked retirement-income eligibility or the amount.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. "Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the coordinators AI Plateau can sort routine repair requests, but it cannot tell from a tidy form how wet a tenant’s ceiling is. I would keep the caretaker’s call in the case before deciding whether to send an emergency plumber.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately I expect a mild tool to leave my manager job and regular salary alone. My wage covers rent and utilities, and we have three months saved; the bicycle shop income varies but is not needed for those fixed bills. I would keep using the triage tool if its priority list matches the actual building.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I would keep the morning call with caretakers on any roof leak marked low priority. I would continue checking the AI triage result against the caretaker’s description before approving a contractor slot. If the mild version arrives next year, I would keep that practice and our ordinary rent payments.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel calm about our basic bills and my job here. I would still be angry if a software label left water running into somebody’s bedroom.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What did a caretaker call change?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: One tenant sent a photograph of a small brown patch, and the triage tool called it routine. The caretaker opened the ceiling hatch and found water running beside a light fitting. We sent an emergency crew that afternoon.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Do you trust the system at all?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Yes, I use it every day to find cases that need a second look. I would not let a low-priority label overrule a person in the building. The tool saves time when we know where it fails.

say: A **routine repair label** cannot replace the caretaker’s report of water damage.
I would keep **building calls** before deciding an emergency slot.
think: My **manager salary** looks steady under mild change and covers fixed bills.
The **three-month reserve** buffers irregular bicycle-shop receipts.
do: **Keep** morning caretaker calls about low-priority roof leaks.
**Compare** existing AI triage with real building reports before approving contractors.
feel: I feel **calm** about basic bills but angry at ignored water damage.
S0.quote: The caretaker opened the ceiling hatch and found water running beside a light fitting.
fieldNote: Her **daily AI use** already includes a caretaker check; this mild scenario continues that routine.
Her **salary covers rent** and utilities, so variable shop receipts do not make basic bills unsafe.

steps.text: Keep calling caretakers about low-priority roof leaks
Compare existing AI priority with caretaker report before booking contractors

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. "Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say stronger AI can schedule routine repairs and draft tenant replies, so the company may try to cover more buildings with fewer coordinators. I would publish missed emergency calls and repeat leaks beside any savings. A cheap repair queue is no bargain for a tenant living under a wet ceiling.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately I think two area managers could be combined, and my post might be one of them. I know the buildings well, but that knowledge may not appear on the cost sheet. Three months saved gives us time to search, not a lasting replacement for my rent-paying wage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Next month I would ask the regional director for a paid six-week check of AI repair priorities against caretaker calls, with my team kept on paid time and an independent surveyor reviewing any dangerous low-priority case. I would run it only after those approvals are in writing. If the offices combine, I would apply for posted housing-service roles only with net pay after travel that covers rent and utilities; I would accept only a confirmed offer with workable hours.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about my post and impatient with cost claims that ignore a tenant’s room. I can test the queue fairly, but I cannot pretend the test guarantees my team’s jobs.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would the surveyor see?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A ceiling patch near wiring and the date of the caretaker’s call. The surveyor can say whether we should have stopped the ordinary queue and sent a specialist. I am not qualified to decide whether the wet ceiling is dangerous without an independent surveyor.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Who would check the paid hours?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My eight coordinators would need time away from the live queue to compare cases. I would not ask them to do it over lunch. The director must approve cover for the live repairs as well as the surveyor’s time.

say: **Repair automation** could shrink coordinator teams while emergencies are missed.
I would publish **repeat leaks** and dangerous delays beside savings.
think: A merger could put my **area-manager post** at risk.
Three months saved cannot replace my **rent-paying wage** for long.
do: **Request** a six-week priority check; run only with approved paid team cover and independent surveyor review.
**Record** repeat leaks and dangerous low-priority cases for the regional director.
**Apply** for posted housing roles only with rent-and-utility net pay after travel and workable hours.
feel: I feel **anxious** about a merger and impatient with unsafe savings claims.
S1.quote: I am not qualified to decide whether the wet ceiling is dangerous without an independent surveyor.
fieldNote: Her **AI test** requires written approval, paid coordinator cover and independent surveyor review.
A **housing move** needs an advertised post, net rent-and-utility pay and actual offer.

steps.text: Apply to posted housing role only with rent-and-utility net pay after travel
Accept only confirmed offer with workable hours

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. "Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell tenants AGI by 2028 could write replies and schedule repairs before there is a clear route to challenge a wrong priority. I would demand written notice for staff and a person who can order an emergency visit when the system misses a live leak.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately I expect the repair desk to lose posts quickly; my manager role could go too. Housing-service reports and contractor schedules are thinking work and face 2028 AGI. Plumbing and lifting a broken door are physical until capable robots arrive around 2031, but I have no trade qualification or promise of a contractor job. Three months saved would go quickly without my salary.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This week I would ask the staff representatives for severance terms and a written human override for dangerous repair requests. I would check rent and utilities against my actual wage, counting only bicycle-shop payments received after parts costs. If AGI arrives in 2028 and I am cut, I would apply for advertised local property roles only if net pay after travel covers rent and utilities; I would accept only a firm offer with hours my partner and I can manage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about losing a job that pays our fixed bills. We have some savings and nearby offices, but I would not call the bicycle shop a substitute manager salary.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Could your partner expand the shop?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Maybe, but I would not put projected repair bookings in our rent budget. Parts have to be bought before customers collect their bicycles. A full shop diary is not the same as money left after the supplier is paid.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What should the override do?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A tenant reports water beside a light fitting, and a named worker can send an emergency crew even if the AI queue says routine. A dashboard cannot dry a live ceiling. The tenant needs a person who can change the priority before nightfall.

say: **2028 AGI** needs a tenant route to challenge wrong repair priorities.
I would seek written **notice and emergency override** for staff.
think: My **own role** could go as repair desks shrink quickly.
Schedules face **2028 AGI**; physical plumbing robots follow around 2031.
do: **Ask** staff representatives this week for severance and dangerous-repair override terms.
**Check** rent and utilities against actual wages and shop receipts after parts.
**Apply** after a 2028 cut only to advertised roles with rent-and-utility net pay after travel.
feel: I feel **anxious** about losing the salary that covers our fixed bills.
S2.quote: A full shop diary is not the same as money left after the supplier is paid.
fieldNote: She counts **net shop receipts**, not bookings, when checking how long three months saved would last.
Physical **repair trades** face robots around 2031 but require qualifications she does not claim.

steps.text: Ask staff representatives for severance and emergency repair override terms
Apply after cut only to advertised property roles with rent-and-utility net pay after travel
Accept firm offer only after checking pay and workable hours

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. "Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say five years lets us test a real tenant visit instead of guessing from a photograph, and to agree who can override a dangerous queue. The company should fund that work rather than send coordinators an unpaid webinar about empathy.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately I could learn to document damp on site, but the inspection report itself faces 2031 AGI just like my desk. Carrying meters and opening ceilings is physical until capable robots around 2034. At 63 I would need to test the stairs and travel, and I do not know what retirement income might actually pay.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: From 2027 I would request one paid supervised tenant visit a month with a qualified damp surveyor. I would attend only if the director approves cover for my live repair queue, I keep my salary and the tenant consents to the visit. After 2031 I would apply for a posted housing-inspection role only with net pay after travel that covers rent and utilities, actual authority to order a repair and site duties I can manage; I would accept only a firm offer.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about my desk, but a supervised visit would show whether I can do the stairs and make a useful report. It would not turn me into a surveyor overnight.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would the surveyor teach?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: How to distinguish a cold surface from water coming through the roof and when to call an electrician rather than touch a wet fitting. I would carry the meter and write the observation, but the surveyor would make the safety decision. I am not certified to sign that report alone.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if the tenant refuses the visit?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: We would not enter. I would ask the surveyor for another case with consent and keep working the live queue. A training target never gives me permission to walk into someone’s home.

say: A **five-year runway** should fund real tenant visits and dangerous-queue overrides.
I would reject **unpaid empathy webinars** as a substitute for practice.
think: Damp reports face **2031 AGI**; physical site work meets robots around 2034.
At **63**, stairs, travel and retirement income remain uncertain.
do: **Request** paid supervised visits from 2027; attend only with queue cover, full salary and tenant consent.
**Apply** after 2031 only for posted inspection work with rent-and-utility pay, repair authority and manageable site duties.
feel: I feel **anxious** about desk loss but able to test physical visits.
S3.quote: A training target never gives me permission to walk into someone’s home.
fieldNote: Her **visit** needs paid time, director-approved queue cover, qualified supervision and tenant consent.
An **inspection vacancy** must pay rent and utilities after travel and grant real repair authority.

steps.text: Attend paid surveyor visit only with director-approved queue cover full salary and tenant consent
Apply after 2031 to posted inspection role only with rent-and-utility net pay and repair authority
Accept only firm offer with manageable site duties and checked hours

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. "Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the company a decade is enough to write down tenant override rights, fund safe inspections and publish the real pay of any new role. A repair queue should be judged by homes made dry, not by messages closed.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately I will be 68 in 2036 and may want to stop working, but I have not checked eligibility or net retirement income. Three months saved is not a lasting wage. Repair reports and contractor schedules face 2036 AGI; physical repair work meets robots around 2039. My partner’s shop may still be uneven.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I would keep caretaker calls and request a verified retirement-income statement, comparing income plus savings with rent and utilities. I would add seventy to savings only after my full salary arrives, the shop’s completed jobs pay after parts costs, and rent and utilities clear. After 2036 I would keep paid work if verified retirement income plus savings cannot cover our bills, and apply to a posted local role if my repair desk ends.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about losing the regular wage at 68 without knowing what retirement pays. I can improve the cash buffer, but the shop’s future diary is not money yet.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why does the shop need to pay first?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A repaired bicycle may wait for collection, while my partner has already paid for the replacement chain. We can count cash only after the customer pays and the parts cost is covered. The extra seventy comes from money left after that and our rent.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you ask the children to cover a gap?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: We would tell them if we were worried, but they have their own households. I do not want a planned monthly payment from them. I want to know the actual retirement terms and our own bill total first.

say: A **decade** should deliver tenant override rights and funded inspections.
I would measure **dry homes**, not closed messages.
think: At **68**, retirement eligibility and net income remain unverified.
Repair reports face **2036 AGI**, with physical repair robots around 2039.
do: **Keep** caretaker calls on leak cases in 2026.
**Save** seventy extra only after full salary, paid shop jobs net of parts, rent and utilities clear.
**Continue** paid work after 2036 if verified retirement income plus savings cannot meet bills.
feel: I feel **anxious** about losing regular wages and unknown retirement pay.
S4.quote: A repaired bicycle may wait for collection, while my partner has already paid for the replacement chain.
fieldNote: Her **new savings** require actual net shop receipts, full salary and cleared rent and utilities.
She makes no **retirement entitlement** or grown-child support assumption despite the ten-year runway.

steps.text: Keep calling caretakers before closing low-priority leak cases
Save seventy only after full salary paid shop receipts net of parts rent and utilities
Continue paid work after 2036 if verified income plus savings cannot meet bills
Apply to posted local role if repair desk ends

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most. The repair desk could shrink before I can find another salary that covers our rent and utilities. Written notice, a human emergency override and a real posted role with adequate net pay would help.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: Ask the tenant whether the ceiling was still wet when our system said the case was closed. A closed repair ticket is not a dry room. I would like the person in that room to have someone they can ring.

headlineQuote: A closed repair ticket is not a dry room.
portrait: **Daria, 58**, is an experienced property-repairs manager supervising eight coordinators.
Her **typical pay**, bicycle-shop partner, three-month reserve and some nearby offices support rented housing.
She uses **AI daily** for repair priorities but checks low-priority leak reports with caretakers.
She is **calm** under mild change, anxious about desk cuts and careful not to count unpaid shop bookings.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could shrink her repairs desk before a rent-and-utility-paying post is available.
whatWouldHelp: Written **notice**, emergency override authority and a posted role with adequate net pay would help.
